overview: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) is a flagship crop insurance scheme launched by the Government of India in Kharif 2016 to provide affordable and comprehensive crop insurance coverage to farmers against non-preventable natural risks from pre-sowing to post-harvest stages. The scheme aims to stabilize farmers' income, encourage adoption of modern agricultural practices, ensure credit flow to the agriculture sector, and promote innovation in insurance products. It operates on an 'Area Approach' basis and is implemented through a multi-agency framework involving insurance companies, financial institutions, and government bodies under the overall guidance of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
objectives: Providing financial support to farmers suffering crop loss/damage arising out of unforeseen events
Stabilizing the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming
Encouraging farmers to adopt innovative and modern agricultural practices
Ensuring credit worthiness of farmers, crop diversification and enhancing growth and competitiveness of agriculture sector
Promoting innovation & research of insurance and allied products to offer expanded choice to farmers and State Governments/UT Administrations
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in a notified area during the season who have insurable interest in the crop are eligible. Compulsory coverage applies to farmers in the notified area who possess a Crop Loan account/KCC account (Loanee Farmers) to whom credit limit is sanctioned/renewed for the notified crop during the crop season, and such other farmers whom the Government may decide to include from time to time. Voluntary coverage may be obtained by all farmers not covered in the compulsory component, including Crop KCC/Crop Loan Account holders whose credit limit is not renewed.
benefits: Financial support for crop loss/damage due to unforeseen events, income stabilization to ensure continuance in farming, encouragement to adopt innovative and modern agricultural practices, ensured flow of credit to the agriculture sector contributing to food security and crop diversification, protection from production risks, and promotion of innovation & research in insurance and allied products. The scheme also provides on-account payment of claims up to 25% of likely claims if expected yield during the season is likely to be less than 50% of normal yield, and claim amount is credited electronically to the individual insured bank account.
financial_support: The Actuarial Premium Rate (APR) is charged under PMFBY by the Implementing Agency (IA). The rate of Insurance Charges payable by the farmer is as follows: 2.0% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less for Kharif foodgrain and oilseeds crops; 1.5% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less for Rabi foodgrain and oilseeds crops; and 5% of Sum Insured or Actuarial rate, whichever is less for Annual Commercial/Annual Horticultural crops. The difference between the premium rate and the rate of insurance charges payable by farmers is treated as the Rate of Normal Premium Subsidy, which is shared equally by the Centre and State. For loanee farmers, insurance charges payable by farmers are financed by the loan disbursing office of the Bank and treated as an additional component to the Scale of Finance for obtaining loan.
application_process: 1. Visit the PMFBY portal at https://pmfby.gov.in and click on 'Farmer Corner' then 'Enroll Now' to apply for crop insurance. 2. Use the Insurance Premium Calculator to know the insurance premium before applying. 3. After enrollment, use the Application Status feature to check your application status on every step. 4. For grievances or to report crop loss, call the Krishi Rakshak Portal & Helpline (KRPH) at 14447. 5. Use the Policy ID to check policy status via the Application Status feature. 6. Access digital tools like Farmer App, WhatsApp Chatbot, AIDE App, CCE App, CLAP App, and WINDS App for application, management, and grievance redressal.
deadlines: Cut-off date for receipt of Proposals of farmers (loanee & non-loanee) is 31st July for Kharif and 31st December for Rabi. Cut-off date for receipt of Declarations of Loanee farmers covered on compulsory basis & non-loanee farmers covered on voluntary basis from Bank branches to Respective Nodal Offices is within 15 working days for loanee farmers and seven working days for non-loanee farmers after cut-off date. Cut-off date for receipt of Declarations of farmers covered on Voluntary basis from designated Insurance Agent(s) to Insurance Companies is within two working days after receiving declaration/premium.

caveats: The scheme is compulsory for loanee farmers obtaining Crop Loan/KCC account for notified crops, but voluntary for other/non-loanee farmers who have insurable interest in the insured crop(s).
Claims for prevented sowing are eligible up to a maximum of 25% of the sum-insured.
Post-harvest losses coverage is available up to a maximum period of 14 days from harvesting for crops kept in 'cut & spread' condition to dry in the field after harvesting.

Localized calamities (hailstorm, landslide, inundation) and post-harvest losses due to specified perils (cyclone/cyclonic rain & unseasonal rains) are assessed at the affected insured field of the individual insured farmer.

The sum insured per hectare for both loanee and non-loanee farmers is the same and equal to the Scale of Finance as decided by the District Level Technical Committee, and would be pre-declared by SLCCCI and notified.
